learning_objective: 🎯 Understand what 'security' truly means in modern times, moving beyond just military threats to include poverty, health epidemics, and human rights!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This focuses on danger from military threats outside a country's borders (external) or civil war within (internal). The main responses are building military strength, deterrence, and forming alliances.

Goes beyond military threats to include human security (protecting individuals from starvation, disease, and natural disasters) and global security (issues like global warming and international terrorism).
Modern threats don't respect national borders. They include terrorism, human rights violations, global poverty, migration/refugee crises, and health epidemics like COVID-19 or HIV/AIDS.
Since new threats like climate change and pandemics cannot be stopped by a single country's military, nations must work together through international cooperation and organizations.

India's strategy involves four components: strengthening military capabilities, strengthening international institutions, meeting internal security challenges, and developing its economy to lift citizens out of poverty.

fun_activity.title: 📰 Headline Hunter
fun_activity.instructions: Look at today's international news headlines. Categorize the top 5 stories as either 'Traditional Security' (e.g., border disputes, military drills) or 'Non-Traditional Security' (e.g., climate summits, disease outbreaks). Which category has more news?

exam_tips: 📌 Always differentiate between 'External' (military threat from another country) and 'Internal' (civil war, separatism) traditional security.
📌 Be ready to explain why poverty and health epidemics are now considered 'security' threats under the non-traditional approach.
📌 Memorize the 4 pillars of India's security strategy, as it's a frequent long-answer question.
quick_recap: ⭐ Traditional security believes the greatest danger to a country is military action from another country.
⭐ Non-traditional security focuses on the protection of ordinary people, not just the state territory.
⭐ Cooperative security emphasizes dialogue and international institutions over military force.
